# Orthodox Church of St. Euphrosyne of Polotsk in Białystok

The Orthodox Church of St. Euphrosyne of Polotsk (Polish: *Cerkiew św. Eufrozyny Połockiej*) is an Eastern Orthodox church located in Białystok, in northeastern Poland.

## Location and Parish
The church is situated in Białystok, a city with a significant Orthodox Christian population, particularly among the Belarusian minority in Poland. It serves as a parish church within the Polish Autocephalous Orthodox Church, falling under the Diocese of Białystok and Gdańsk.

## Patron Saint
The church is dedicated to St. Euphrosyne of Polotsk (c. 1110–1173), a medieval Belarusian princess, nun, and abbess who is one of the most venerated saints in the Eastern Slavic Orthodox tradition. She is particularly important to Belarusian Orthodox Christians, making her an especially fitting patroness for a church serving a community with strong Belarusian heritage.

## Significance
Białystok and the surrounding Podlasie region have one of the largest concentrations of Orthodox Christians in Poland, and the city contains several Orthodox churches. Each parish typically serves specific neighborhoods of the city.

Białystok has multiple Orthodox churches (including the better-known Holy Spirit Church, St. Nicholas Cathedral, and others), and detailed information about smaller parish churches may not be well-documented in my sources.
